subject: Discovery recap: index scale, latency targets & POC next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightleaf.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: index scale, latency targets & POC next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — good first conversation. Below is a short recap so we’re all aligned and I’ve captured the initial asks + next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain & goals
- Current pain: inconsistent relevance on reranking layer for long-tail queries; expensive per-query costs from current setup.
- Goal: reduce rerank latency and unit cost while keeping or improving hit-rate on NDCG-based metrics for the top-5 results.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Vector DB: FAISS (self-hosted, custom HNSW indexes) for production; Pinecone used for experiments.
- Embeddings: in-house transformer (768-d) batched nightly for full re-index; realtime embedding pipeline for user queries (~30ms per embed).
- Index scale: ~350M vectors currently, expected to grow to ~450M in 9–12 months.
- Traffic profile: 10k QPS (search) peak across regions; rerank path receives ~1.2k QPS, mostly small batches or single-query real-time.

Success criteria (what will make this a win)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end rerank < 150ms (target), p99 < 300ms (escalation threshold).
- Cost: reduce per-query infrastructure cost on rerank by ~30% vs current spend.
- Quality: maintain or improve top-5 NDCG on the evaluation set you shared.
- Ops: straightforward rollout path (canary, A/B) and telemetry to detect regressions.

Preliminary technical constraints
- Data residency: production indexes must remain in customer VPC (private deployment for POC is ok).
- KV cache expected for prefix reuse on conversational flows.
- Need encryption-at-rest and SOC2 evidence (you sent the questionnaire).

Proposed POC scope & timeline
- Objectives: validate throughput/latency at 350M vectors, quantify cost delta for rerank path vs your baseline, and run evals on your sample prompt set (we’ll use the NDCG kit you shared).
- Duration: 2 weeks of controlled runs + 1-week buffer for tuning (total 3 weeks).
- Deliverables: benchmark report (latency/cost), configuration recipe for production, and a canary rollout plan.

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses)
- Send POC outline and minimal test dataset (Vanessa) — attached: redwood-poc-outline.pdf, redwood-quick-compare.csv.
- Complete security questionnaire and staples (BrightLeaf) — will use brightleaf-security-questions.xlsx and return answers.
- Solutions deep-dive to size cluster (Connor) — Connor will propose instance types and quantization profile for 350M index.
- Confirm logistics & contract/term guardrails (Tom / Vanessa) — discuss trial credit and data handling.

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule the POC kickoff next week and loop in engineering for the setup. Thanks again — excited to dig in.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (application/pdf, 87 KB)
Attachment: redwood-quick-compare.csv (text/csv, 12 KB)

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightleaf.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 16:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: index scale, latency targets & POC next steps

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap and aligned on the priorities. A few clarifications from our side:
- Index scale: we’re at ~325M unique vectors today (I rounded up on the call), but will cross 400M within ~8 months.
- Traffic: peak of 10k QPS was across our entire product; the rerank traffic you quoted (~1.2k) matches our telemetry for the rerank microservice.
- Latency targets: p95 < 120ms would be ideal (we’ll take <150ms as acceptable for the POC), p99 < 250ms if possible.
- Cost: internal budget target is to keep incremental cost for rerank under $12k/month initially while we validate.

We’ll start returning the security questionnaire by EOD Tuesday. Tom and I are available for kickoff next Wed/Thu — either day works. For the POC dataset, I can share a 2M-query eval set and a small subset of production index slices (~50M vectors) if that helps for tuning before a full run.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Lena
Head of Search & Relevance
BrightLeaf Analytics
---
Attachment: brightleaf-security-questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 45 KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightleaf.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: index scale, latency targets & POC next steps

Connor / Dylan / Marissa — looping you in formally. Quick asks based on Lena’s clarifications:
- Connor: prepare a sizing proposal for a 350M index (we’ll treat 325M as the baseline but size for 400M headroom). Include quantization options (int8 / 4-bit), expected memory per shard, and recommended instance families. Note: they prefer private deployment (VPC) for the POC.
- Dylan: can you sketch a test plan to validate p95 < 120ms (target) and p99 < 250ms? Include telemetry points (tokens, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate) and the canary rollout steps.
- Marissa: be ready to propose a trial credit + terms outline and confirm who owns the SOC2 artifacts we’ll share. Also flag any legal or compliance gates for private deployments.

I’ll schedule a 30m sync for Tuesday 10:00 AM PT to review Connor’s sizing and Dylan’s test plan — invite forthcoming. Lena / Tom: does Tuesday 10:00 PT work for you for a quick technical kickoff? If not, shoot alternative times.

Thanks — Vanessa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
